home.introduction: ProcessPuzzle/... is a set of libraries to easy building of an Angular application. It helps with very low level tasks like application initializing or **Low-Code** plattform for generating tables and CRUD forms run-time from entity descriptors.
home.utils_card_content: This is a collection of functions, services and components useful when building Angular applications. The package contains:
home.utils_card_content_1: runtime-configuration - reads the application runtime, at app initialisation
home.utils_card_content_2: app-initializer - service which helps by application initialization
home.utils_card_content_3: layout-service - to help by responsive layouts
home.widgets_card_content: This is a collection of UI components useful when building Angular UI. The package contains:
home.widgets_card_content_1: Back Button - navigates back to the previous page
home.widgets_card_content_2: Like Button - enables to count fans for the page
home.widgets_card_content_3: Share Button - facilitates to share a link to the application with others
home.auth_card_content: This is a collection of UI components and services for authentication and authorisation. The package contains:
home.auth_card_content_1: Auth Button - menu for authentication actions
home.auth_card_content_4: Registration Component - facilitates user to register
home.auth_card_content_5: My Profile Component - enables to review and change user profile data
home.auth_card_content_6: Auth Service - helps to authenticate users
home.auth_card_content_7: Auth Guard - support authorisation true routes
home.base-entity_card_subtitle: Base classes for reactive forms and material tables
home.base-entity_card_content: Facilitates of building full functional Forms and Tables with connection to data source and support of Signal Store stage management from simple Entity Definition.
home.base-entity_card_content_1: Generate Angular Material Table with filter, search and paging capabilities
home.base-entity_card_content_2: Generate full flagged reactive form with checks and error messages
home.base-entity_card_content_3: Generate state dependent header to navigate from table to form and back
home.base-rule_card_subtitle: Declarative business rules at design and run-time
home.base-rule_card_content: Provides a uniform way to define, import, export and evaluate business rules over your domain objects without scattering conditions through the code base.
home.base-rule_card_content_1: Define rules in YAML and load them as RuleDefinitions
home.base-rule_card_content_2: Evaluate objects against rule sets and collect violations
home.base-rule_card_content_3: Import and export rule catalogues between environments
home.base-document_card_subtitle: Wiki-style textual documents as first-class entities
home.base-document_card_content: Provides the Angular constructs needed to describe, edit and render the documents a Low-Code application works with — an ordered list of text and widget blocks, together with their metadata.
home.base-document_card_content_1: Describe a document by title, description and typed input/output ports
home.base-document_card_content_2: Edit page content as a list of blocks, with widgets embedded in the text
home.base-document_card_content_3: Store documents and their block structure server-side through base-document-backend
home.base-state_card_content: Models the life-cycle of your domain objects as explicit state machines, so transitions, guards and side-effects become first-class citizens.
home.base-state_card_content_1: Declare states and allowed transitions for an entity
home.base-state_card_content_2: Guard transitions with rules and pre-conditions
home.base-state_card_content_3: Drive UI behaviour from the current state of the entity
home.base-workflow_card_content: Composes activities, decisions and waits into long-running workflows that coordinate entities, rules and states across users and systems.
home.base-workflow_card_content_1: Describe workflows as a sequence of tasks and gateways
home.base-workflow_card_content_2: Persist and resume workflow instances across sessions
home.base-workflow_card_content_3: Integrate with rules and state machines for decisions
home.base-ai_card_subtitle: Recognise known objects in photos and videos
home.base-ai_card_content: Identifies enrolled objects — a sailboat by its sail number, a vehicle by its plate — in photos and videos, without retraining a model for every new object.
home.base-ai_card_content_1: Author recognition profiles: detector class, identifier and matching thresholds
home.base-ai_card_content_2: Enroll objects with a gallery of photos, read and checked against their identifier
home.base-ai_card_content_3: Runs detection, OCR and appearance matching on a shared vision server
home.base-app_card_subtitle: Compose entities, rules, states and workflows into a running application
home.base-app_card_content: Describes a whole application as metadata — its workspace, navigation and panel layout — then builds it and promotes it so users can reach it under its own route.
home.base-app_card_content_1: Edit the application definition: workspaces, navigation and panel layout
home.base-app_card_content_2: Assemble entity, rule, state and workflow modules into the application shell
home.base-app_card_content_3: Build and promote the application under /appRoute/orgKey
home.test-utils_card_subtitle: Utilities for unit- and integration testing
home.test-utils_card_content: This is a collection of functions and services to easy unit- and integration testing.
home.test-utils_card_content_1: mock-breakpoint-observer - help to test responsive pages. Imitates resizing of a page.
home.test-utils_card_content_2: transloco-testing-module - sets up Transloco for testing Component with i18n capabilities.
home.test-utils_card_content_3: layout-service - to help by responsive layouts
home.ci-cd_card_subtitle: GitHub Actions base continuous delivery process
home.ci-cd_card_content:
This isn't a library, but an end-to-end solutions for continuos delivery pipeline, base on GitHub Actions.
            It supports multiple quality assurance practices und multiple development stages. At the end delivers increments automatically to production.
home.ci-cd_card_content_2: Supports deploy to AWS or Firebase
home.ci-cd_card_content_3: Supports to publish to NPM registry

base-rules.samples_desc_1: The following sample entities demonstrate the capabilities of the rule engine:
base-rules.samples_desc_2: Pick a sample below to explore how rules are defined and evaluated against it.
base-rules.samples_edit_hint: The rules evaluated on these forms are authored in the Design section:
base-rules.intro_paragraph_1: The ProcessPuzzle Rule Engine lets Low-Code applications author, evaluate and visualize business rules. It combines a set of Angular building blocks for the user interface with a Spring Boot backend that stores and executes the rule definitions.
base-rules.intro_paragraph_2: The engine is split into two complementary libraries which share a common domain vocabulary:
base-rules.intro_frontend_desc: Angular services, stores and components used to design, edit and visualize rules in the browser.
base-rules.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that persists rule definitions and evaluates them on the server side, following the platform's Hexagonal architecture.

base-documents.samples_desc_1: Documents are wiki-style textual content — project plans, design docs, reports — composed of a flat, ordered list of text and widget blocks.
base-documents.samples_desc_2: The table and form below are generated run-time from the Document descriptors; the Content tab opens the block editor.
base-documents.intro_paragraph_1: ProcessPuzzle Document Management gives a Low-Code application a place to keep its textual content, described by the same kind of metadata as every other entity: a title, a description and typed input and output ports. A document's body is a flat, ordered list of blocks — either Tiptap-editable rich text, or a widget reference resolved against the same registry the app shell uses.
base-documents.intro_paragraph_2: The feature is split into two complementary libraries which share a common domain vocabulary:
base-documents.intro_frontend_desc: Angular services, stores and components to describe, edit and render documents in the browser.
base-documents.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that stores documents and their block structure server-side, following the platform's Hexagonal architecture.

base-states.samples_desc_1: A state machine describes the life-cycle of a domain entity: its states, the transitions between them and the guards on those transitions.
base-states.samples_desc_2: The table and form below are generated run-time from the State Machine Definition descriptors; states and transitions are embedded components of the machine.
base-states.intro_paragraph_1: ProcessPuzzle State Machines model the life-cycle of your domain objects explicitly, so that transitions, guards and side-effects become first-class citizens rather than conditions scattered through the code base.
base-states.intro_paragraph_2: The feature is split into two complementary libraries which share a common domain vocabulary:
base-states.intro_frontend_desc: Angular services, stores and components to declare states, resolve the allowed transitions and drive the UI from the current state.
base-states.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that persists state and transition definitions and resolves transitions on the server side.

base-workflows.samples_desc_1: A workflow composes activities, decisions and waits into a long-running whole that coordinates entities, rules and states across users and systems.
base-workflows.samples_desc_2: The tables and forms below are generated run-time from the Workflow, Tool and Workflow Instance descriptors; roles, work products and tasks are embedded components of a workflow, and the instance screens are read-only.
base-workflows.intro_paragraph_1: The ProcessPuzzle Workflow Engine executes long-running business workflows: it advances a workflow instance as facts arrive, assigns the resulting tasks and keeps the history of why an instance reached its current step.
base-workflows.intro_paragraph_2: The feature is split into two complementary libraries which share a common domain vocabulary:
base-workflows.intro_frontend_desc: Angular services, stores and components to describe workflows and monitor running instances in the browser.
base-workflows.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that persists workflow definitions and executes workflow instances on the server side.

base-ai.samples_desc_1: Image recognition tells which of a list of known objects is in front of the camera: a sailboat by its sail number and its look. Each object brings its own photos; recognition matches what the camera sees against them.
base-ai.samples_desc_2: The screens below are the framework's generated screens; the Recognition tab is contributed by base-ai onto every entity type that has a recognition profile, and the camera is base-ai's widget hosted by a page of this app.
base-ai.samples_step_1: Open the Recognition Profile. The seeded "boat" profile says how boats are recognised: the reference photos are the boat's "photos" attribute, the detector looks for the "boat" class, and the sail number is read from the "sailNumber" attribute and must look like three letters and up to five digits.
base-ai.samples_step_2: Switch to Boat, open CAN 603, the 49er "Maple Leaf", and on its Details tab add photos to Photos and save. To try it right away, download this photo of CAN 603:
base-ai.samples_step_3: Open its Recognition tab: each photo is processed in the background — on a CPU about 10 to 30 seconds — and shows the crop of the boat and the sail number read on it. The same photo on another boat, say GER 1234, is flagged as differing from the registered number.
base-ai.samples_step_4: Switch to Race: two races are seeded, Autumn Regatta 2026 with three rounds and Club Championship 2026 with two.
base-ai.samples_step_5: Switch to Registration and enter boats: some in the Autumn Regatta, others in the Club Championship. A race's registrations are the constraint of recognition — only its entries can be recognized.
base-ai.samples_step_6: Switch to Recognize, choose a race, a round and a checkpoint, point the camera at a boat — or pick the photo — and press Recognize. The hit is saved as a Race Observation of that context; a boat the camera missed is ticked by hand.
base-ai.samples_step_7: Change the race, round or checkpoint: the candidates and the list of boats seen follow the context. Race Observation lists every sighting, by the camera or by hand.
base-ai.intro_paragraph_1: ProcessPuzzle Image Recognition tells which of a given list of known objects — boats, vehicles, people — is in front of the camera, without retraining a model for every new object. An object brings a handful of photos of its own; from then on it is recognised by an identifier painted on it, such as a sail number, and by its appearance. What the answer is used for is the application's business.
base-ai.intro_paragraph_2: The feature is metadata-driven like every other ProcessPuzzle feature: which entity type is recognised, by which detector class and identifier, with which thresholds, is a Recognition Profile — data, not code. It is made of three parts:
base-ai.intro_frontend_desc: Angular screens to author recognition profiles, the Recognition tab that shows what recognition made of an entity's photos, and the camera widget that recognizes an object among candidates.
base-ai.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that owns profiles, galleries and recognitions, keeps a gallery in step with its object's photos and talks to the vision server.
base-ai.intro_vision_desc: Python service running the models — detection, tracking, OCR and appearance embeddings — on CPU, shared by every application stack.
base-ai.recognize_no_entries: No boat is registered for this race yet — enter some under Registration.

base-apps.samples_desc_1: An application definition describes a whole application as metadata: its navigation, routes, regions, widgets and the modules it mounts.
base-apps.samples_desc_2: The table and form below are generated run-time from the App Definition descriptors, exactly like any other entity.
base-apps.intro_paragraph_1: ProcessPuzzle Application Designer assembles the other features into something a user can open: it describes the application shell as metadata, then builds and promotes it so users reach it under its own route.
base-apps.intro_paragraph_2: The feature is split into two complementary libraries which share a common domain vocabulary:
base-apps.intro_frontend_desc: Angular services, stores and components to edit the application definition and render the shell that hosts everything else.
base-apps.intro_backend_desc: Spring Boot module that persists application definitions and serves them to the shell at run-time.
